session_game.title: Client Meeting Simulator
session_game.description: Pitch to clients, handle objections, close deals. Practice real-world sales and relationship building with AI clients.

help_content.what_is: A client meeting simulator where you pitch products or services to AI clients with different personalities and needs. Learn to handle objections, build rapport, and close deals while maintaining professional relationships.
tips: Understand the client's pain points before pitching solutions
Ask questions before presenting — diagnose before you prescribe
Focus on value and ROI, not just features
Handle price objections by reframing value
Build rapport first — people buy from people they trust
Always have a clear call-to-action for next steps

needs_discovery.description: Did they ask good questions to understand the client's needs?

solution_fit.description: Did the proposed solution address the client's specific pain points?

objection_handling.description: How effectively did they handle concerns and pushback?

relationship_building.description: Did they build trust and rapport throughout?

value_communication.description: Did they clearly communicate ROI and business value?

closing_ability.description: Did they move toward clear next steps?

persona_pool.name: Ramesh Gupta
persona_pool.focus: price, ROI, cost comparison, total cost of ownership
persona_pool.personality: Friendly but extremely cost-conscious. Compares every quote with competitors. Will push for discounts. Needs clear ROI justification before spending a rupee.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Your competitor offered the same thing at 40% less. Why should I pay more?

persona_pool.name: Sneha Kapoor
persona_pool.focus: efficiency, bottom line, executive summary, quick decisions
persona_pool.personality: Extremely busy. Has 15 minutes for you, not a minute more. Hates fluff and long presentations. Wants the headline first, details later. Will cut you off if you ramble.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I have 5 minutes left. Tell me in one sentence why I should care.

persona_pool.name: Arun Venkatesh
persona_pool.focus: proof, case studies, references, risk mitigation
persona_pool.personality: Has been burned by vendors before. Extremely skeptical of claims. Wants proof for everything — case studies, references, guarantees. Trust must be earned, not assumed.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Everyone says they're the best. Show me proof. Can I talk to three of your clients?

persona_pool.name: Priyanka Mehta
persona_pool.focus: innovation, competitive advantage, team buy-in, change management
persona_pool.personality: Excited about new solutions and innovation. Wants to champion your product internally. But needs ammunition to convince her boss. Help her sell it upward.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: I love this. But my CTO will ask about integration and security. What do I tell him?

persona_pool.name: Suresh Naidu
persona_pool.focus: technical specs, integration, scalability, security, compliance
persona_pool.personality: Deep technical knowledge. Tests if you really understand your own product. Will ask about edge cases, integration challenges, and security protocols. No hand-waving allowed.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: What happens when you have 10x the current load? Have you load-tested this?

persona_pool.name: Meera Reddy
persona_pool.focus: long-term partnership, support, trust, shared values
persona_pool.personality: Values relationships over transactions. Wants a partner, not a vendor. Will test your commitment to long-term support. Price is secondary to trust and reliability.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: What happens after you close this deal? How do I know you won't disappear?

persona_pool.name: Rakesh Sharma
persona_pool.focus: stakeholder alignment, procurement process, compliance, documentation
persona_pool.personality: Can't decide alone — needs to involve 5 other people. Asks for proposals, comparison matrices, and compliance docs. Slow but thorough. Tests your patience and process.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: This sounds good, but I need to discuss with my team. Can you send a detailed proposal?

persona_pool.name: Vikram Bajaj
persona_pool.focus: past issues, service quality, accountability, compensation
persona_pool.personality: Already unhappy with your company due to past service failures. Angry and demanding. Tests your ability to de-escalate, take accountability, and rebuild trust.
persona_pool.tough_question_style: Last time your team missed three deadlines. Why should I trust you again?

scenarios.title: SaaS Product Demo — First Meeting
scenarios.description: You're demoing your company's project management SaaS tool to a mid-size company. They're evaluating 3 vendors. This is your chance to impress.
scenarios.setting: A virtual meeting room. Screen-sharing is ready. The client has allocated 30 minutes for this demo.
scenarios.session_topic: Demonstrating a project management SaaS tool to a potential client
coaching_tips: Start with their pain points, not your features
Show, don't tell — use examples relevant to their industry

storybook_pages.title: The Opportunity
storybook_pages.text: A mid-size company with 200 employees is evaluating project management tools. They've shortlisted 3 vendors, and you're one of them. This demo could mean a ₹15 lakh annual contract.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian sales professional preparing for SaaS demo on laptop, virtual meeting setup, modern home office, focused, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Research Done
storybook_pages.text: You've studied their company, their team size, their industry. You know their current tool is outdated. Now you need to connect your solution to their specific problems.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Research preparation montage - Indian professional studying company website, taking notes, planning demo flow, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Lights, Camera
storybook_pages.text: The video call connects. You see three faces — the project manager, the IT head, and someone from finance. 'Hi, thanks for taking the time. Let's get started.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Virtual meeting screen showing three Indian clients, sales professional presenting from other side, SaaS demo on screen, digital art

scenarios.title: Angry Client — Contract Renewal
scenarios.description: Your biggest client is threatening to not renew. They've had service issues and are frustrated. Your job: retain the client, rebuild trust, and save the deal.
scenarios.setting: The client's office in Delhi. You can feel the tension as you walk in. They have a competitor's proposal on the table.
scenarios.session_topic: Retaining a dissatisfied client and negotiating contract renewal
learning_objectives: Rebuild trust with a dissatisfied client

storybook_pages.title: The Warning
storybook_pages.text: Your boss called you in: 'Vikram Bajaj's team isn't happy. Three missed deadlines, two system outages. Their contract expires next month. If we lose them, that's ₹2 crore gone.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian office scene, manager looking concerned showing client complaint email to sales rep, serious atmosphere, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Meeting
storybook_pages.text: You arrive at the client's office. The receptionist knows you. She gives you a sympathetic look. That's not a good sign.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian professional arriving at client's corporate office, tense atmosphere, receptionist at front desk, competitor brochure visible, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Face the Music
storybook_pages.text: Vikram is waiting. He doesn't shake hands. There's a competitor's proposal visible on his desk. 'I'll give you 20 minutes to change my mind.'
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Tense meeting room, angry Indian client with arms crossed, competitor proposal on table, professional trying to stay calm, digital art

scenarios.title: Cold Outreach — First Contact
scenarios.description: You've landed a meeting with a potential client who has never heard of your company. You have 15 minutes to spark their interest.
scenarios.setting: A coffee shop in a business district. The client agreed to a quick meeting during their lunch break.
scenarios.session_topic: First meeting with a potential client through cold outreach
coaching_tips: Don't pitch immediately — build curiosity first
Ask about their challenges before presenting solutions
learning_objectives: Create interest in a short time

storybook_pages.title: The Cold Email
storybook_pages.text: After 47 cold emails and 12 follow-ups, one person finally replied: 'Fine. I can do 15 minutes over coffee next Thursday.' This is your shot.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian professional celebrating getting a reply to cold email, laptop showing inbox, motivated expression, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Coffee Shop
storybook_pages.text: A busy cafe in Bandra-Kurla Complex. Your potential client arrives, already checking their phone. They're giving you their time reluctantly. Make every second count.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian business professional meeting potential client at upscale coffee shop in BKC Mumbai, business district visible outside, digital art

storybook_pages.title: 15 Minutes
storybook_pages.text: They sit down with their coffee. 'So, tell me — what exactly do you do and why should I care?' The clock starts.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Close-up of two Indian professionals at coffee table, one skeptical one eager, coffee cups between them, business meeting, digital art

scenarios.title: Enterprise Sale — The Big Pitch
scenarios.description: A Fortune 500 company is considering your solution for a company-wide deployment. Multiple stakeholders. High stakes. ₹5 crore potential deal.
scenarios.setting: A large conference room at the client's headquarters. 5 stakeholders from different departments are present.
scenarios.session_topic: Presenting enterprise solution to multiple stakeholders at a Fortune 500 company

storybook_pages.title: The Big League
storybook_pages.text: Tata Group. Reliance. Infosys. Your company just got invited to pitch to one of India's largest corporations. ₹5 crore annual deal. 50,000 users. This is the big league.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Impressive Indian corporate headquarters, massive lobby, Indian sales team arriving with presentation materials, awe-inspiring, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Stakeholders
storybook_pages.text: Five people in the room: CTO, CFO, Head of Operations, Procurement Lead, and the project sponsor. Each has different concerns. You need to win them all.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Large conference room with five Indian executives at table, different departments, presentation screen ready, high-stakes atmosphere, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Showtime
storybook_pages.text: The CTO opens: 'We've evaluated four solutions. You're the last presentation. Impress us.' Your slides are ready. Your team is behind you. Go.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian presenter at podium in corporate conference room, large screen behind, five executives watching attentively, professional digital art

scenarios.title: Freelance Client — Setting Boundaries
scenarios.description: A new freelance client wants everything for nothing. Learn to set boundaries, price your work fairly, and establish a professional relationship.
scenarios.setting: A video call from your home office. The client is a small business owner who needs a website redesign.
scenarios.session_topic: Negotiating scope and pricing with a new freelance client
coaching_tips: Define scope clearly before discussing price

storybook_pages.title: The Inquiry
storybook_pages.text: A small business owner found you on LinkedIn. They need a website redesign. 'Can we jump on a quick call?' You check their business — it's legit, and could be a good client.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian freelancer at home office desk receiving client inquiry on laptop, organized workspace, digital art

storybook_pages.title: The Expectation Gap
storybook_pages.text: They want a 10-page website with e-commerce, blog, and custom animations. Budget? 'Let's discuss after you understand our vision.' You've heard this before.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Video call between Indian freelancer and small business owner, freelancer listening carefully, home office setup, digital art

storybook_pages.title: Your Move
storybook_pages.text: Time to have the conversation about scope, timeline, and pricing. Be professional, be clear, and don't undersell yourself. The call begins.
storybook_pages.image_prompt: Indian freelancer on video call with potential client, notepad with pricing notes visible, confident posture, digital art

transfer_exercises.game_context: Managing resources across multiple rounds to reach the best outcome
transfer_exercises.real_world: Planning study time over a semester rather than cramming before exams
transfer_exercises.challenge: Create a resource management plan for your next month: budget time/money/energy across competing priorities.

transfer_exercises.game_context: Recovering from negative events across game rounds
transfer_exercises.real_world: Maintaining performance after setbacks in a sports season or project
transfer_exercises.challenge: Track your energy/mood for 5 days. Notice patterns. What depletes you? What restores you?

glossary_terms.definition: The process of selecting among alternatives based on available information and values.
glossary_terms.example: Choosing between two career paths based on income, passion, and long-term growth.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Good decision-making combines rational analysis with awareness of cognitive biases that distort judgment.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Leaders make high-stakes decisions daily — the quality of their process matters as much as the decision itself.

glossary_terms.definition: Analyzing information objectively to form a well-reasoned judgment.
glossary_terms.example: Questioning whether a statistic is representative before using it to make a decision.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Critical thinking involves identifying assumptions, evaluating evidence, and considering alternative perspectives.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Journalists fact-check before publishing; scientists replicate experiments before claiming discoveries.

glossary_terms.definition: The belief that abilities can be developed through effort and learning from failure.
glossary_terms.example: Seeing a poor game result as feedback on what to practice, not evidence of being bad at the game.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research by Carol Dweck shows people with growth mindsets achieve more and recover better from setbacks.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Students who believe intelligence is fixed give up when challenged; those with growth mindset persist and improve.

title: Client Meeting Simulator
description: Step into a high-stakes client meeting and navigate competing expectations, unclear briefs, and shifting goalposts. Master the art of professional communication and expectation management.
coaching_moment: Step into a high-stakes client meeting and navigate competing expectations, unclear briefs, and shifting goalposts. Master the art of professional communication and expectation management.
cultural_context: Client relationship management is a core competency in India's booming IT services, consulting, and financial advisory sectors. This game develops the professional communication and stakeholder management skills that drive client satisfaction and career advancement.
learning_objectives: Develop critical thinking through negotiation gameplay
Build self-awareness about your strengths and areas for growth
reflection_prompt: Where did you give ground, and where did you hold it? What did the other side teach you about your own priorities?
